papers.title_en: OmniQEC: discovering practical quantum error-correcting codes by an AI scientist
papers.authors: Ge Yan, Shanchuan Li, Pengyue Ma, Qixin Zhang, Pingchuan Ma, Jianping Wang, Min-Hsiu Hsieh, Yuxuan Du
papers.evidence: 直接针对量子纠错码发现，并包含基于解码器的评估
papers.tldr: 量子纠错是容错量子计算的关键，但发现有效QEC码颇具挑战，因逻辑性能取决于码结构、硬件、症候提取与解码之间的复杂权衡。OmniQEC以大型语言模型为编排者，结合自进化推理与快慢双环工作流，迭代执行码生成、代码级筛选、症候提取综合与电路级评估。在四个qLDPC构造族、三个LLM后端及14个物理比特预算设置下，发现的码持续提升逻辑错误抑制，并在98与240物理比特预算下超越[72,12,6]和[144,12,12] BB码。该工作展现了LLM辅助、物理信息驱动的码-电路-解码器协同设计路径，为实用QEC实现提供了硬件友好的新方案。
papers.abstract_en: Quantum error correction (QEC) is indispensable for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing. However, discovering QEC codes that remain effective is challenging, as logical performance depends on the interplay between code structure, hardware, syndrome extraction, and decoding, which often impose competing requirements. Here we introduce OmniQEC, an efficient AI scientist for discovering QEC codes suited to deployment on modern quantum processors. OmniQEC formulates QEC design as an iterative discovery process in which an orchestrator, implemented by advanced large language models (LLMs), coordinates code generation, code-level screening, syndrome-extraction synthesis, and decoder-based circuit evaluation. At its core, OmniQEC combines a self-evolving reasoning mechanism with a slow--fast synergistic workflow: a fast loop explores candidates using inexpensive code-level proxies, whereas a slow loop performs physically grounded circuit-level evaluation and feeds the resulting evidence back into the search. We evaluate OmniQEC across four qLDPC construction families, three LLM backends, and $14$ total-physical-qubit budgets per backend. The discovered codes show steadily improving logical-error suppression with increasing physical-qubit budgets and outperform the BB codes with $[\![72,12,6]\!]$ and $[\![144,12,12]\!]$ under complete-implementation budgets of 98 and 240 physical qubits, respectively. The discovered codes are hardware-friendly and may be of independent interest for practical QEC implementation. These findings pave the way towards LLM-assisted QEC discovery grounded in physically informed code--circuit--decoder co-design.

papers.title_en: Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Locally Recoverable Codes: Characterizations, Bounds, and Constructions
papers.authors: Yang Li, San Ling, Zhenliang Lu, Gaojun Luo, Shixin Zhu
papers.evidence: 引入纠缠辅助量子局部可恢复码，基于稳定子形式构造的新型量子纠错码。
papers.tldr: 量子局部可恢复码(qLRCs)通过少量量子位即可纠正擦除，但标准构造对底层经典码施加双包含或自正交约束，限制了经典LRCs的应用。为此引入纠缠辅助量子局部可恢复码(EAQLRCs)，假设预共享纠缠对一半无噪，刻画扩展稳定器的支持条件，并给出无需双包含的CSS-like构造。进一步建立局部性上界和Singleton-like界，刻画达到等号的纯码，并基于MDS码的ℓ-交集对与块奇偶校验矩阵构造两族最优纯CSS-like EAQLRCs。这是首批显式EAQLRCs家族，为从经典LRCs灵活构造量子LRCs提供了通用框架。
papers.abstract_en: Quantum locally recoverable codes (qLRCs) allow a single qudit erasure to be corrected by accessing only a small number of other qudits. Standard CSS and Hermitian constructions, however, impose dual-containing or self-orthogonal constraints on the underlying classical codes, thereby restricting the well-structured classical LRCs (cLRCs) that can be used to construct qLRCs. To relax these constraints, we introduce entanglement-assisted quantum locally recoverable codes (EAQLRCs) by assuming that halves of the pre-shared maximally entangled pairs are noiseless. We characterize sufficient support conditions on extended stabilizers under which entanglement-assisted stabilizer codes have locality $r$ and derive a CSS-like construction from two classical codes without imposing the ordinary dual-containing condition. We further establish an upper bound on locality and a Singleton-like bound for arbitrary CSS-like EAQLRCs, and characterize the pure codes attaining equality in the latter bound. These results yield a general framework for constructing optimal pure EAQLRCs from pairs of cLRCs. Applying this framework to $\ell$-intersection pairs of MDS codes and block parity-check matrices, we obtain two families of optimal pure CSS-like EAQLRCs with flexible parameters and nontrivial localities. To the best of our knowledge, these represent the first explicit families of EAQLRCs.
